problemStatement.formal: Can every integer $N\geq 2$ be represented as a ratio of consecutive products \(\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(m+i)/\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n+i)\) with $k\geq 2$ and $m\geq n+k$? For fixed $n,k$, what can be said about the set of integers represented this way?
problemStatement.plain: Can every integer at least 2 occur as an integer ratio of two same-length consecutive-product blocks?
whyMatters: The formalization connects consecutive products to factorials and binomial coefficients.
